title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 737 of the continuation of La Longue Marche. It opens §2, 'Enveloppes schématiques des L-groupes', with subsection 1° 'Notion de L-groupe, de LT-groupe (cas discret)'.

Why the section exists. The previous page studied Fermat curves F_n through the 2-dimensional torus G = G_m^{{0,1,∞}}/G_m. Grothendieck concluded that the approximation used there is 'beaucoup trop grossière', i.e. essentially abelian: it only sees Q-points of the torus, not the Fermat equation. He says one must pass to finer approximations. §2 is meant to supply them, through 'schematic envelopes': pro-algebraic or Malcev-type completions of fundamental groups that carry loop structure.

What the page does, in modern terms.
- A 'groupe à lacets' (from the Longue Marche) is a discrete group Π with an extra structure. Π is isomorphic to π_1 of an oriented surface of finite type (g,ν), i.e. X∖S with X compact and S finite. The structure is a family of conjugacy classes of 'loop' subgroups, isomorphic to Z, given by the punctures; these are the peripheral subgroups, with their oriented generators.
- An 'L-groupe' is the natural generalisation. It should cover 'mixed' fundamental groups of such surfaces equipped with a finite group of automorphisms. In modern terms these are orbifold fundamental groups, or extensions 1→Π→E→G→1 with G finite.
- Key lemma recalled: if Π is a loop group and Π_0 ⊂ Π has finite index, then Π_0 inherits a loop structure. Its loop subgroups are the intersections Π_0∩L, with L running over the loop subgroups of Π. Topologically this is the induced structure on a finite covering surface.
- The N.B.: a loop structure is determined by the family of conjugacy classes of its cyclic loop subgroups, except in the degenerate types (g,ν) = (0,0) and (0,1). There π is {1} or Z, and the data does not pin down the structure. The next page says only (0,1) causes trouble for the induction argument.
- Programme continued on the next page:
  - Conversely, the structure on Π can be recovered from the structures on its finite-index subgroups.
  - Let L_0(π) be the set of admissible loop structures, excluding (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0).
  - These sets form an inductive system over finite-index normal subgroups π_i.
  - L_0^{G_i}(π_i) is the set of structures invariant under G_i = π/π_i.
  - An L-groupe is then a discrete group that is virtually a loop group, with a compatible, invariant germ of loop structure on its finite-index subgroups.
- The 'enveloppes schématiques' announced in the title, presumably pro-algebraic completions of such L-groups, are not yet reached on this page.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The degenerate cases are flagged correctly: in types (0,0) and (0,1), a loop structure is not determined by conjugacy classes of cyclic subgroups.

A small subtlety is left implicit. On restriction, Π_0∩L is a finite-index subgroup of L ≅ Z. Its 'generator' is a power of L's generator, so the induced loop set comes from Π_0-conjugacy classes, i.e. orbit splitting. This is routine but not spelled out.
The type (1,0) (torus) is excluded from L_0 on the next page. On this page the N.B. lists only g=0, ν∈{0,1} as problematic, so the two exclusion lists are slightly inconsistent.

ideas.what: Groups with loop structure (groupes à lacets): surface groups of type (g,ν) carrying peripheral conjugacy classes of oriented cyclic subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Surface groups with peripheral structure; group pairs (π,{peripheral subgroups}); profinite analogues in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, 1981); classical in 3-manifold and Fuchsian-group theory
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated; partial edition by Malgoire)

ideas.what: L-groups: generalisation to fundamental groups of surfaces with a finite group of automorphisms, defined via compatible invariant loop structures on finite-index subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental groups of 2-orbifolds / virtually surface groups with peripheral structure; Fuchsian groups with torsion
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the Longue Marche; this axiomatisation via inductive systems L_0^{G_i}(π_i) is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: Induced loop structure on finite-index subgroups, and recovery of the structure from finite-index subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Peripheral structure of a finite cover; commensurability invariance of peripheral structure

ideas.what: Schematic (pro-algebraic) envelopes of L-groups, proposed as a finer, non-abelian approximation for studying rational points such as those of Fermat curves
ideas.modern_name: Malcev / pro-unipotent / relative (weighted) completion of fundamental groups of curves and orbifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, P^1∖{0,1,∞}); Hain (relative and weighted completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto; M. Kim (non-abelian Chabauty, 2005)

missed.claim: Read with the previous page, this section shows Grothendieck explicitly moving from an 'abelian' approximation (the torus/Jacobian level) for rational points on Fermat curves to schematic (pro-algebraic) envelopes of fundamental groups with loop/orbifold structure. That is essentially the strategy of Minhyong Kim's non-abelian Chabauty method, which uses unipotent fundamental groups as successively finer approximations to Selmer/section sets. It also parallels Hain's relative completion of orbifold groups.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents an early (c. 1981) Grothendieck plan to use pro-algebraic completions of (orbifold) fundamental groups as finer-than-abelian approximations to Diophantine section problems. It predates Deligne 1989 and Kim 2005 and is not credited in that literature. The insistence on keeping loop/inertia structure and finite automorphism groups in the envelope may suggest variants, e.g. completions relative to inertia, not standard in Kim's set-up.

missed.claim: There is a definitional framework for L-groups and LT-groups: groups with a germ of loop structure that is invariant on finite-index normal subgroups. It is set up as the prelude to defining their schematic envelopes. Whether the construction of these envelopes is completed lies beyond this page.
missed.quote: La notion de L-groupe est la généralisation naturelle de celle de "groupe à lacets", qui s'impose si on veut pouvoir englober des groupes fondamentaux mixtes de surfaces orientables ... avec groupe fini d'automorphismes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An intrinsic, commensurability-invariant axiomatisation of orbifold surface groups with peripheral data, designed for completion functors. It could be compared with modern treatments of profinite/pro-ℓ orbifold groups in anabelian geometry, e.g. Mochizuki and Hoshi on cuspidalization and inertia.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is definitional and mostly routine. Its interest is programmatic: with the previous page, it shows Grothendieck proposing pro-algebraic envelopes of orbifold fundamental groups as a non-abelian refinement for rational-point problems, anticipating the Deligne–Hain–Kim line. The theme of non-abelian approximation in anabelian geometry is known in spirit, which keeps the score moderate.
transcription_corrections: In the N.B., the unreadable passage likely reads roughly '[N.B. On a vu que ceci est valable sauf dans les cas (g,ν) avec g=0, ν∈{0,1}, où la structure à lacets n'est pas déterminée par la seule donnée d'une famille de classes de conjugaison de sous-groupes (≃Z)'. 's-groupes' means 'sous-groupes'.
'le {+seul+} cas qui ici ferait pb': 'seul' is written above 'cas' as an insertion; the line reads 'le seul cas qui ici ferait pb'.
The header '737' is the original page number; the archive page is 178.
